title: Beef and Chicken Cottage Pie with Mushrooms
description: Ground beef and chicken breast simmered in a thick mushroom gravy under a creamy cheddar mash, with the filling made ahead at lunch.

ingredients.name: Worcestershire sauce
ingredients.note: use 3 if skipping Better Than Bouillon

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.note: optional, only if filling is loose

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and cubed; or half Yukon Gold, half russet

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: for the potato water and to taste

steps.title: Lunch prep: mushrooms
steps.text: Finely chop {mushrooms}. Cover and refrigerate.

steps.title: Lunch prep: potatoes
steps.text: Peel and cube {potatoes}. Submerge in cold water in a covered container and refrigerate so they do not brown.

steps.title: Lunch prep: cheese
steps.text: Shred {cheddar} if it is not pre-shredded. Refrigerate.

steps.title: Start the filling
steps.text: Melt {butter} and {oil} in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the chopped mushrooms and cook 6 to 8 minutes, until they release their liquid and it evaporates.

steps.title: Brown the meat
steps.text: Add {beef} and {chicken}. Break up and brown for 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in {garlic}, {onion}, and {tomatopaste}. Cook 1 to 2 minutes, until the paste darkens slightly.
Sprinkle in {flour}, stir to coat everything, and cook 1 minute to remove the raw flour taste.

steps.title: Build the gravy
steps.text: Add {beefbroth}, {chickenbroth}, {worcestershire}, {aminos}, and {btb}.
Stir in {thyme}, {umami}, {paprika}, and {blackpepper}.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, 12 to 15 minutes, until thick enough to hold a trail when a spoon is dragged through it. A thick gravy is the goal.
If the filling is still loose, whisk {cornstarch} into {water}, stir it in, and simmer 2 minutes.
Off heat, stir in {acv}. Taste and add {salt} only if needed.

steps.title: Cool and hold
steps.text: Cool the filling uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes, then cover and refrigerate until dinner. This can sit all day.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the Anova Precision Oven to 400°F in dry bake mode with no steam and the bottom drip pan installed.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Boil the cubed potatoes in generously salted water with {salt} for 15 to 18 minutes, until fork-tender.
Drain well and return the potatoes to the dry hot pot for 1 minute to steam off excess moisture.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Mash the potatoes with {tbutter}, {creamcheese}, {milk}, {garlicpowder}, and {tpepper}. Add a splash more milk if needed for a smooth, spreadable mash.
Stir the shredded cheddar into the mash.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Reheat the filling on the stovetop until hot throughout, then spread it into a 9x13 baking dish.
Spread the mash over the filling all the way to the edges to seal it in. Rough up the surface with a fork for extra browning.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the filling bubbles at the edges and the top is golden.
For deeper browning, run the top element (broil) for the last 2 to 3 minutes, watching closely.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest 5 to 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Make the whole filling at lunch and dinner is just boil, mash, assemble, and bake (about 40 minutes). Flour is bumped to 3 tablespoons from 2 for a gravy that clings. Taste before baking since no salt is added to the filling; Worcestershire, coconut aminos, and Better Than Bouillon carry most of it. The filling freezes well on its own, so consider doubling it and freezing half for a near-instant cottage pie with fresh mash.
